cells.good_for: Repeatable checks for relevance, correctness, style, safety, or schema requirements
cells.limit: A poorly defined rubric produces misleading scores

cells.good_for: Scalable semantic evaluation when exact string matching is inadequate
cells.limit: Judge bias/variance requires calibration and representative examples

cells.good_for: Nuance, high-impact decisions, and calibration of automated evaluation
cells.limit: Slower and more expensive; needs clear reviewer guidance

cells.good_for: Structured evaluation of supported model/application quality dimensions
cells.limit: Still choose representative data and decision thresholds

prompts.label: SEPARATE RAG FAILURES
prompts.placeholder: Reveal what to measure at each layer. A bad final answer can originate in retrieval or generation.

cells.measure: Whether relevant/authoritative evidence is retrieved and ranked well
cells.failure: Tune source sync, chunking, embeddings, filters, query, search mode, or reranking

cells.measure: Precision, source coverage, duplication, freshness, and usefulness of supplied context
cells.failure: The generator is being given noisy, stale, or missing evidence

cells.measure: Groundedness, factuality, relevance, citation/source use, and task correctness given good context

cells.failure: Use layer metrics to localize the root cause before changing components

cells.meaning: Whether needed evidence appears in the candidate set

cells.symptom: Top results contain distractors or unrelated chunks

cells.meaning: Whether best evidence is placed early enough to reach the model
cells.symptom: Correct evidence exists but appears below noisy results

cells.meaning: Operational cost of the retrieval stage
cells.symptom: RAG is correct but slow before generation even begins

cells.meaning: Whether the index reflects current source data
cells.symptom: Recently updated documents cannot be found

Run the retrieval/search step directly and inspect candidate/reranked chunks

prompts.label: INSPECT AN APP TRACE RECORD
prompts.placeholder: Click the correlation, prompt/model version, retrieval evidence, and latency fields. This is an application trace example, not a fixed AWS-native schema.

annotations.title: Application request correlation
annotations.explanation: A stable request identifier lets application logs and evaluation artifacts point to the same execution without relying on timestamps alone.

annotations.title: Distributed trace correlation
annotations.explanation: A trace identifier can connect the GenAI request to downstream services and dependencies such as APIs, retrieval, and tools.

annotations.title: Prompt version
annotations.explanation: Version the prompt/template so an intermittent failure can be reproduced against the exact instruction set used in production.

annotations.title: Model identity
annotations.explanation: Record the model or routed target used for the request; model changes can alter output behavior even when the prompt is unchanged.

annotations.title: Retrieved evidence
annotations.explanation: Correlating retrieved chunks helps distinguish a retrieval failure from a generator failure.

annotations.title: Per-stage latency
annotations.explanation: Stage-level timing localizes performance problems instead of treating total response time as a single opaque number.

prompts.label: 🎯 EXAM CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Exam trap to avoid: __________

reveal.text: Without version and trace correlation, intermittent GenAI failures are difficult to reproduce.
